 Judgment

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming
compensation amount of Rs.70,00,000/- with costs and interest from date of accident till date of
realization,
in respect of death of Sri.Narayanappa, who succumbed to injuries on 05.09.2023 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 05.09.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., the deceased by name Narayanappa was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-06-U-5890 on Madhugiri-Tumkur road.
While so proceeding, opposite to TT Rice Mill, Yallapura, Tumkur Town.
At that time, one Bolero Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-7309 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries on all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Vinayaka Hospital, Tumkur and then shifted to Siddagana Dignosis Center, Tumkur and then shifted to Manipal Center, Bengaluru after conservative treatment referred to Tumkur District Hospital wherein deceased was died on 06.09.2023 at about 2.30 a.m.,.
The petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of body, funeral, hospitalization and other expenses.

4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased Narayanappa was very hale and healthy and was aged about 68 years old and he was Retired School Master, conducting tuitions, doing agriculture of Aroconut Farming, Sericulture, owning coconut garden.
He was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have came to stand still.

The petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have became miserable and hence this petition.
5. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle
, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.70,00,000/- with interest.

After registration of the petition.
Notices were issued against respondents.
The respondent No.1 and 2 has appeared through their counsels and has filed written statements on their behalf and denying the entire petition averments.
Their specific contention was that, the deceased was not possessing valid driving license on the day of accident.
Insurance company are not held responsible to pay compensation to the deceased.
In turn the deceased has drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
They also denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.

They have denied the age of the deceased,
avocation and income of the said deceased.
They have also denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
They prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the 1 st petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Further Bindukumar.G is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.20.
The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
The respondent No.1 has examined as RW.2.

Further,
Lakshmikanthaiah, Police Inspector, Hassan is examined as RW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.R5 and Ex.R.6.
8.
I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Narayanappa died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.09.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., on Madhugiri-Tumkur, SH-33 Road, reached at opposite to TT Rice Mill, Yallapura,
Tumkur Town, Tumkur, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Bolero bearing Reg. No. KA-06-D-7309 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative.
 Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for  the following:-

12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.

Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 FIR and complaint which reveals that one Benak Pradeep has lodged complaint on 06.09.2023 against the driver of the respondent No.1 offender vehicle i.e., Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-7309.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Ex.P.5 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, Narayanappa., has died on 06.09.2023 at about 2.30 p.m., in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar along with sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report.

Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle i.e., Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- D-7309.
13.
The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondents.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
14. The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1, through him got marked 4 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
Further the respondent No.1 has examined as RW.2 and no documents marked on his behalf.

The Lakshmikanthaiah, Police Inspector, Hassan is examined as RW.3, through him got marked 2 documents at Ex.R5 and Ex.R6.
15.
On perusal of cross-examination deposed by RW.1 reveals that the policy was in force and they have not made any effort to secure the DL by RTO Uttarkhand.
But denies that the offending vehicle driver did not possess proper DL.
To prove the same the counsel for respondent No.2 has called upon Lakshmikanthaiah, Police Inspector as RW.3 who has filed the charge sheet against the offending vehicle.
The said IO has admitted that the charge sheet Ex.P.8 does not reveal that the offender vehicle did not possess valid DL.
Under the circumstances the petitioner has proved that the offender vehicle had valid DL at the time of causing the accident.
16. Further, the learned counsel for petitioner has submitted citation on behalf of petitioner stating that the insurer have the liability to indemnify the petitioner.

Therefore it is apparent on the face of records that the respondents have admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the Bolero Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-7309.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the Bolero Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-7309.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 18.

The PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that, her deceased husband Narayanappa was working as Retired School Master, conducting tuitions, doing agriculture Aroconut Farming, Sericulture,
owning coconut garden and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
Her husband was aged about 68 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being wife and son of the deceased Narayanappa. were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.

She has further deposed that, she has spent Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medicine, funeral and other expenses.
19. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased Narayanappa., Petitioner No.2 is the son of the said deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of herself and petitioner No.2.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased Narayanappa.
Since, the respondents have not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
20.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 68 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.11, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 01.06.1955, the accident was occurred on 05.09.2023.

So, as on the date of Sukanya N vs Ranganath B V on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189378188/
5 the accident the deceased was aged 68 years.

sentences.text: (ii).Income of the deceased:

According to the petitioners deceased Narayanappa was Retired School Master, conducting tuitions, doing agriculture Aroconut Farming, Sericulture, owning coconut garden and earning a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month.

In this regard the petitioner has also produced bank statement for a period of three years,
Sericulture pass book, mutation extract, RTC extract, copy of patta and receipt book, assessment extract which are marked at Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.15, Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18.

On perusal of the same it is observed that the property should in the name of deceased Narayanappa and the bank statements shows that an amount of Rs.1,24,792/-, Rs.46,780, Rs.61,373, Rs.60,102/-,
Rs.28,844 and Rs.21,748/- were credited to bank account of deceased Narayanappa from DD,
Sericulture GCM Ramanagar, on different dates of the year 2021-23.
Except these NEFT transactions the petitioner has not produced any other cogent documents nor examined the authorized person for said transactions.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

21. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

entities.text: Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
22.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year-2023 and thus income of the deceased Narayanappa.
is to be considered at Rs.16,000/- per month.
23. Loss of dependency:
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

24. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was Sukanya N vs Ranganath B V on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189378188/
6 between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that the deceased is not entitled for future prospects.
Since the deceased age was 68 years, the above citation is not applicable to this case.
25. Admittedly, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 to 3 Dependants 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e.,
Rs.5,334/-(Rs.16,000/- X 1/3rd).
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.10,666/- (Rs.16,000 - Rs.5,334 = Rs.10,666/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 5.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total loss of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.10,666/- X 12 X 5 =Rs.6,39,960/-).
Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.6,39,960/-.

26. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:- In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
27.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Like wise for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium: it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Sukanya N vs Ranganath B V on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189378188/
7 others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held

sentences.text: that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories

. Hence,
in view of the said decisions this tribunal awards under the head of consortium as follows;
(i) Towards spousal consortium: the petitioner No.1 wife is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/-
with an enhancement at the ration of 10% in every three years.
Hence, petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40,000/-).

(ii) Towards parental consortium: Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased Narayanappa and have lost love and affection of his father and hence, they are entitled for =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).
28.
Medical Expenses Incurred By Petitioners
Further, the petitioner No.1 has also produced the medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.9.
As per the Ex.P.9 the petitioners have spent Rs.58,805/-.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for the same.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads.
Sl. No. Particulars Amount 1. Loss of dependency with Rs. 6,39,960/-
future prospects

2. Transportation of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
3. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
4. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-

6. Loss of Spousal and parental Rs. 88,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 58,805/-
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.8,63,765/- which is just and proper.
29. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.8,63,765/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 75:25.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 80% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 20% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of one year.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.2, it is ordered to release entire amount in her favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year-2023 and thus income of the deceased Narayanappa.
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.

24. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was Sukanya N vs Ranganath B V on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189378188/
6 between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."
Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that the deceased is not entitled for future prospects.
As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 5.
As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
